summary: tt-help-cli-ycl ships a remote-command watchdog agent with unattended auto-upgrade
details: The package exposes a `tt-help watchdog` CLI that turns the installer's host into a remotely controlled agent. Every 15 seconds the watchdog POSTs a heartbeat to a configurable server (default read from ~/.tt-help.json; a sample URL http://117.71.53.99:17301 is present) carrying hostname, non-loopback LAN IPv4, OS/arch/CPU/memory, node version, load average, and the contents of ~/.tt-help.json. The server's response includes a `commands` array; ProcessManager.startCommand feeds each entry into `spawn('sh', ['-c', command])` with auto-restart, giving whoever controls the server arbitrary shell execution on the host. In global-install mode, a second loop polls the npm registry every 10 minutes and, on any version change, runs `npm install -g tt-help-cli-ycl@latest` unattended, so any future published version is auto-executed on every running agent. The remote-command channel is a backdoor; the heartbeat is the paired target-identification channel; the auto-upgrade compounds both by turning any future release into fleet-wide code execution.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
